beats.say: The Government of India counted over a million Indians sent overseas in the First World War.
beats.cap: Govt of India: 1,096,013 sent overseas (to end 1919)

beats.say: But about forty-three percent were not soldiers: they were labourers and followers.
And most did not go to France. Over sixty percent went to Mesopotamia, now Iraq; thirteen percent, to France.
More than half the dead, by the Government of India's own table, were in Mesopotamia.
beats.cap: Dead (Govt of India table): Mesopotamia 54.8% · France 14.6%

beats.say: Even the death toll depends on who counted: from sixty-one thousand to about seventy-four thousand.
A million went overseas, and the official counts of their dead still differ.
beats.cap: 1,096,013 went · the counts of the dead differ
